Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Incidents

Incidents

SATOM's own tickets (SAT-INC-…) for operational problems — opened by hand or by a runbook at the end of its run — with a history of every change and the tickets opened with a vendor or L3, each with its own history.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced userOperator
🔑 Permissionsoperations.view operations.apply
📍 WhereOperations → Incidents in every ADOM (URL /incidents/)

  • What does it do?

What is it?#

An incident is SATOM's ticket for an operational problem: a device that does not answer, a failover, a recovery. It carries a permanent reference of the form SAT-INC-000001, an appliance, a severity (P1–P4), a status and an owner.

These are not Sentinel's incidents. Sentinel's (INC-…, Operations → Sentinel) are security incidents built from attack events; they stay in their own console.

What does it do?#

  • Opens from a runbook. A Plugin Studio app with an Open incident step (see Apps) raises one at the end of each run: open when the problem is not solved, resolved when the run fixed it, so the record stays either way. The summary is the run's steps and the page links the run. A run opens one incident, never two.
  • Opens by hand. New incident on the list: title, severity, appliance and a summary.
  • Keeps a history. Every note and every change of status, severity or owner is a line with who made it and when. Nothing is deleted: an incident opened by mistake is closed with a note. Resolving or closing stamps the time; reopening clears it.
  • Keeps the vendor's and L3's tickets. On the incident's page you add the tickets opened with a vendor or L3 (Fortinet TAC, your L3 team): ticket number (it can come later), a link to the vendor's portal and what was reported. Each ticket has its own history and status (open, waiting vendor, waiting us, resolved, closed). An incident can have several.

Statuses of an incident: open, in progress, waiting vendor, resolved, closed.

Permissions#

  • View operations (operations.view) opens the list and the incidents.
  • Run operations (operations.apply) opens incidents and changes them: notes, status, severity, owner and vendor / L3 tickets.
  • Every change is also a line in the Audit Log (incident.*).

The list shows only the incidents of the appliances the current ADOM sees, plus those tied to no appliance. Global shows them all.

How to use#

  1. Operations → Incidents.
  2. Search by reference, title, appliance, summary, owner or vendor ticket number, and filter by status (Active = not yet resolved), severity, appliance, who opened it (a runbook or a person) and dates. The filters stay in the URL, so a filtered list can be bookmarked.
  3. Open an incident. On the right, Update sets the status (with an optional reason), the severity and the owner.
  4. Add a note for anything worth keeping: what was tried, who was called.
  5. When you open a ticket with the vendor or L3, Add a vendor / L3 ticket: who it is with, the number, the link (https:// only) and what you reported. When they answer, write it in the ticket's line, change its status or add the number, and press Record.

Limits#

  • No company ticket system (ServiceNow, Jira…) is connected yet. The incident shows Company ticket: not linked.
  • SATOM does not read or write the vendor's portal: the ticket's number, status and history are what you record.

Troubleshooting#

A runbook run finished but no incident appeared#

Possible causes — the run was a simulation (Simulate or Cover every branch): the Open incident step then only says "simulation: would open an incident (…)" and creates nothing. Or the run ended on a path without an Open incident step.

Solution — run the app armed, or add the step before the end the run reached (Plugin Studio › the app › Diagram).

"this run already opened SAT-INC-…"#

Possible causes — the step was walked again by the same run (a resumed run, or a loop back in the diagram). A run opens one incident.

Solution — nothing to do: open the incident named in the message.

"the ticket link must start with http:// or https://"#

Solution — paste the web address of the vendor's ticket, or leave the link empty and record only the number.

"nothing to record: write what happened or change the status"#

Solution — a vendor-ticket update needs a text, a new status, or both.

An incident I expect is not in the list#

Possible causes — the list only shows incidents of appliances your ADOM sees (plus those tied to no appliance), and the filters are kept in the URL.

Solution — clear the filters, or open the list from the ADOM that holds the appliance.

#incident#ticket#SAT-INC#vendor ticket#TAC#L3#escalation#runbook#recovery#history#severity#owner
